metaDescription: Six padded tub transfer benches compared by cushion material, seat size, swivel or slide and weight rating, for bathers who find hard plastic cold and slippery.
introParagraphs: Most transfer benches are molded plastic over aluminum. The seat is easy to clean and rarely wears out, but it is also cold on contact, slick when wet and unforgiving for anyone with little padding of their own. A padded transfer bench replaces the hard plastic with a cushioned seat and often a cushioned back and arms, which warms the first touch and spreads pressure. The tradeoff is that padding needs to shed water and dry, or it becomes a maintenance problem.

The six picks here use different padding. The Medline Padded and the Drive Medical Padded use cushioned seats and backs on aluminum frames rated to 400 lb, the VMS uses microcell polyurethane foam at 300 lb, and the Platinum Health Carousel and Roundabout 2.0 use closed-cell polyurethane on sliding swivel benches. The Medline Combination adds a commode opening and bucket to a padded bench.

We evaluated each from listing specs and buyer feedback, not from hands-on lab work. We pay attention to how each pad is described, since closed-cell and microcell foams shed water while open cell foams do not, and to how the bench is used, because a slide or swivel changes how much of the seat the user actually touches.

products.name: Medline Padded Transfer Bench for Bathtub and Shower, 400 lb
products.description:
The Medline Padded is the all-round pick. It has a padded backrest and seat, a side arm for extra stability, a reversible backrest for either side of the tub and a 400 lb rating on a rust-resistant aluminum frame weighing 11 lb. Seat height adjusts by push button from 18 to 22 inches, and the seat measures 24 by 16 inches.

The listing gives the overall footprint as 32 inches wide and 25.5 inches deep, with a height including the backrest of 32 to 36 inches. That is a larger footprint than the plain Medline, which is the price of the padding and arm. Wide suction cup feet add security inside the tub and slip-resistant feet hold outside.

Assembly is tool-free with locking push buttons. It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the VMS it has a higher rating and an arm, and compared with the Platinum benches it is fixed and simpler. Choose it for a padded, armed, fixed bench. Set the bench up with the legs at the same step, check the suction cups inside the tub and press the arm and seat with a firm push. Wipe the cushions dry after each bath and let them air out.
products.bestFor: Users who want a padded fixed bench with a side arm.
pros: Published dimensions and a reversible back

products.name: Drive Medical Padded Shower Seat Chair for Bathing
products.description:
Drive Medical's padded bench uses a lightweight aluminum A-frame with a cushioned seat and backrest, rated to 400 lb. It has one open side so it can function as a bath transfer seat, a handle that moves to the right or left and non-skid leg tips with superior traction on wet surfaces. Dual-column extension legs adjust in half-inch increments through built-in pinch-free push pins.

The listing gives the overall dimensions as 19.75 inches deep by 29 inches wide with the seat at 24 by 16 inches and a height of 17.75 to 21.75 inches. Those numbers make it a mid-size bench that fits most standard tubs. The cushioned seat is warmer than plain plastic, and the half-inch steps let you match the tub rim closely.

It sits in the lower-middle of the price range. Compared with the Medline Padded it has finer height steps and a smaller footprint but no side arm. Choose it for a padded bench with precise height. Match the half-inch steps to the tub rim, check the pinch-free pins have clicked and move the handle to the entry side. Wipe the cushion and dry the leg tips after bathing.
products.bestFor: Standard tubs where a cushioned seat and half-inch height steps matter.
pros: Handle can move to either side

products.name: VMS Padded Transfer Bench, 300 lb
products.description:
The VMS is a lighter-duty padded bench with a waterproof, tear-resistant microcell polyurethane foam cushion. It has a generous 26.25 by 16.25 inch seat, a reversible back to suit any bathroom layout, height adjustment and tool-free assembly, on a lightweight aluminum frame that supports up to 300 lb.

Microcell foam is a closed structure that sheds water better than open foam, and the listing calls it tear-resistant. The seat is wider than the Medline Padded's, which gives more room. The 300 lb rating is the lowest in the group, which limits it to lighter users.

The listing does not publish an overall footprint or a height range in the material we reviewed, so check the product page. It sits in the lower part of the price range. Compared with the Medline Padded it is wider and cheaper but rated lower. Choose it for a lighter user and a wide padded seat. Check the product page for the overall footprint before ordering, since it is not in the listing text we reviewed. After assembly, wipe the foam dry and watch for any tear along the edge.
products.bestFor: Lighter users who want a wide padded seat at a low cost.
cons: 300 lb capacity is the lowest here
Height range and footprint not in the material we reviewed

products.name: Platinum Health Roundabout 2.0 Sliding Transfer Bench with Rotating Seat
products.description:
The Roundabout 2.0 is a professional-grade sliding bench with a padded rotating seat. The padding is medical-grade closed-cell molded polyurethane that the listing says will not absorb water and is easy to clean. The swivel seat protrudes into the room less than a traditional bench, and the high-contrast Hi-View blue color helps users with poor vision distinguish the chair from its surroundings.

The listing describes smooth, effortless transfers in and out of the tub and a design used in hospitals and nursing homes as well as private homes. A rotating seat means the user does not have to swing their legs over the wall, and the padding adds warmth. The listing does not state a weight rating in the material we reviewed.

It sits at the top of the price range. Compared with the Carousel it is the newer model. Choose it for a padded swivel slide with a high-contrast color. Check the dimensions in the listing images against your tub, practice the slide and rotate with a helper and wipe the closed-cell pad dry after use. Keep the rotating mechanism clean of soap film.
products.bestFor: Users who need a padded slide, a swivel and high-contrast color.
cons: No weight rating in the material we reviewed

products.name: Platinum Health Carousel Sliding Shower Chair Tub Transfer Bench
specs: Padded swivel seat, back and arms
products.description:
The Carousel pads every main component, with warm, slip-resistant closed-cell polyurethane on the seat, back and armrests. The swivel seat is described as safer, easier and more comfortable than a fixed seat, the padded arms pivot and serve as leverage points, and the backrest reclines. The bench is fully reversible for left or right entry.

The listing stresses that the arms are weight-bearing and robust, which sets it apart from many benches that have no arms. It also warns to review the dimensions in the thumbnail images before ordering, to make sure it fits both the user and the tub. No weight rating appears in the material we reviewed.

It sits near the top of the price range. Compared with the Roundabout 2.0 it adds arms and a reclining back. Choose it when full padding and arms are the goal. Review the thumbnail dimensions carefully before you order, set up the reversible bench for your entry side and test the arms in each position. Wipe the padded arms and seat dry after every bath.
products.bestFor: Users who want padding on the seat, back and arms with a swivel.
pros: Padding on seat, back and arms
cons: No weight rating in the material we reviewed
Costs near the top of the range

products.name: Medline Padded Combination Transfer Bench and Commode, 400 lb
products.description:
This Medline is a padded bench with a commode cutout and a side arm, rated to 400 lb. It comes with a pail, a lid and a splash guard, which makes it a bedside toilet as well as a tub transfer seat for users who cannot reach a bathroom quickly. Suction cup feet add stability, and the adjustable seat height is 18 to 22 inches with a seat depth of 16 inches.

Combining the two functions saves space and equipment for households with limited room. The padding and the side arm are the same comfort features as the padded bench. The tradeoff is more parts to clean and a bench that is designed for two uses at once.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the Medline Padded it adds a commode function. Choose it when one piece of equipment has to serve two purposes. Clean the pail, lid and splash guard separately from the bench, and keep the commode function dry and covered between uses. Wipe the padded seat and arm after use, and check the suction cups.
products.bestFor: Households that need a padded bench that also works as a commode.
pros: Commode cutout with pail, lid and splash guard
cons: Dimensions beyond the seat are not in the material we reviewed

buyingCriteria.criterion: What the padding is made of
buyingCriteria.explanation: The Platinum benches use medical-grade closed-cell molded polyurethane that the listings say will not absorb water, the VMS uses waterproof microcell polyurethane foam and the Medline and Drive benches use cushioned seats and backs. Closed and microcell foams shed water and wipe clean, while open foams can hold moisture. Look for a surface that dries quickly, and wipe it after every use. A pad that feels slightly too soft on first sitting may also be a pad that wears quickly.

The VMS offers 26.25 by 16.25 inches, the Medline Padded 24 by 16 and the Drive Padded 24 by 16. A wider seat is more comfortable and more forgiving of an imperfect slide. A deeper seat helps a taller user. Check that the bench's width suits your tub, since a wide padded seat can overhang a narrow rim. If the user has trouble with a hard edge, a deeper seat reduces pressure at the knee.

The Medline and Drive padded benches are fixed, requiring the user to shuffle across. The Platinum Roundabout and Carousel slide and rotate, with a helper's assistance. Padding helps most on a fixed bench where the user sits and moves, and on a swivel where the user stays seated. Choose by the user's ability. Padded surfaces collect soap film, so rinse as well as wipe.

The Medline Padded has a side arm, the Carousel has pivoting padded arms and a reclining backrest, and the Drive has a handle. Arms give leverage for sitting and standing. A padded arm is gentler on the hands than a bare metal bar. Decide where the user needs support. Padded arms are useful, but check that they are firm enough to push on.

The Medline Padded is 32 by 25.5 inches overall, the Drive Padded 29 by 19.75. Padded benches tend to be larger because of the cushions and arms. Measure the clear floor beside the tub and the rim width. The Platinum listing warns you to review dimensions before ordering. Leave room for a helper to stand beside the bench.

Padding must be wiped and dried after each use, or it can develop odors and wear. The Platinum listings say the padding is easy to clean, and the VMS foam is tear-resistant. Avoid abrasive cleaners that can damage the cover. Replace any pad that cracks or peels. Replace worn pads before they crack.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pad material and water behavior
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared closed-cell polyurethane on the Platinum benches, microcell foam on the VMS and cushioned seats on the Medline and Drive. Surfaces that shed water and wipe clean scored higher. A surface that stays dry stays cleaner.

howWeEvaluated.title: Seat room
howWeEvaluated.description: We read seat dimensions of 24 by 16 and 26.25 by 16.25 inches and noted which listings do not publish them. A wider, deeper seat earned credit for comfort. A wide seat is more comfortable, but only if it fits the tub.

howWeEvaluated.title: Transfer style
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated fixed padded benches from the sliding swivel Platinum models and noted the padded arms on the Carousel. Padding is only as good as the structure under it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We recorded 400 lb on three picks, 300 lb on the VMS and no stated figure on the Platinum benches in the material we reviewed. A missing rating counted as a gap for the buyer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered drying, cleaning and pad replacement. Closed-cell and microcell pads were credited for durability. Daily upkeep made the difference between close calls.

faq.q: Does padding make a transfer bench less safe?
faq.a: Not if the pad is firm enough and the bench is stable. A very soft pad can feel unsteady, so look for a surface that holds its shape and does not slide. The pad should stay put on the seat.

faq.q: How do I clean a padded bench?
faq.a: Wipe the pad with a mild cleaner after each use, dry it and let it air out. The Platinum listings say the closed-cell padding is easy to clean. Avoid abrasive cleaners that can crack the cover.
Yes, eventually. Replace the pad or the bench if it cracks, peels or becomes sticky. A tear-resistant foam like the VMS's microcell foam lasts longer. Keep it dry between uses.

faq.q: Is a padded bench worth the extra space?
faq.a: If hard plastic is cold and uncomfortable for the user, yes. Padded benches are larger because of the cushions and arms, so measure first. A wider seat is easier to sit on.

faq.q: What is the difference between closed-cell and open foam?
faq.a: Closed-cell foam has sealed bubbles that do not absorb water, while open foam can soak water. For a bathroom, closed-cell or microcell is better. The Platinum benches use closed-cell polyurethane.

faq.q: Can I use a padded bench as a commode?
faq.a: Only the Medline Padded Combination has a commode cutout, with a pail, lid and splash guard. Other benches are designed for bathing. Do not improvise a commode from a regular bench.

faq.q: Should I put a towel on a hard bench instead?
faq.a: A towel can add warmth, but it slides, holds water and can bunch under the user. A purpose-made padded seat is safer. If you do use a towel temporarily, remove it before sliding and do not use it on a sliding or swivel seat.
